Appendix G
ARCHAEOLOGICAL AND HISTORICAL SITES
The 1972 survey conducted by University of Montana archaeologists (Dale & Lynn Fredlund) for Westmoreland Resources was the first full scale archaeological survey ever made in advance of actual mining activities in the Sarpy Creek country. In Westmoreland Tract III, generally located within Townships 1 North, and 1 South, and Ranges 37, & 38 East, Big Horn County, Montana, the following archaeological sites were found and given identification numbers:
24BH1070  A cluster of 9 vision quest cairns on a high point overlooking Sarpy Creek near the old John Luther homestead.
24BH1071  A small lithic materials area (rock flaking) but no intact artifacts.
24BH1072  A small lithic materials area with few artifacts.
24BH1073  A small lithic materials area with no artifacts.
24BH1074  A small camp site with heavy concentration of lithic materials; 8 inch test pits produced several artifacts.
24BH1075  A brief period habitation site, 300 by 25 feet area with few artifacts found.
24BH1086  Temporary habitation site, 300 by 200 yards area scattered with lithic materials.
